title: SOP for Analysis of α-Cypermethrin in Biological Samples by Gas Chromatography
author: Ram Dhakal
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.y8ifzue
materials: Cap and vortex each sample for 1 min.

steps.title: Label Tubes and Vials
steps.instruction: Label disposable culture tubes and GC vials using unique sample numbers including initials and experiment identifiers. Prepare the following:

substeps.instruction: At least one tube for method blanks (water only).
At least one tube for sample blanks (matrix from unexposed or vehicle-exposed animals).
Three tubes for Ongoing Precision and Recovery (OPR) samples (matrix from unexposed or vehicle-exposed animals).
Tubes for all experimental samples (recommended 20% QA/QC samples).
One tube for the Reference Standard.

steps.title: Prepare Initial Sample Aliquots
steps.instruction: Add the following materials to the prelabeled tubes:

substeps.instruction: Method blanks: 200 μL of water.
Sample blanks: 200 mg of clean sample matrix.
OPR: 200 mg of clean sample matrix per tube.
Experimental samples: 200 mg of each sample per tube.

steps.title: Spike Samples with Standards
steps.instruction: Add surrogate standards to the tubes as follows:

substeps.instruction: Spike 100 µL of 1 µg/mL cis/trans-permethrin in acetonitrile (100 ng each per sample) to every tube, including the Reference Standard.
Spike 100 µL of 1 µg/mL α-cypermethrin in acetonitrile (100 ng per sample) to the three OPR tubes and the Reference Standard (do not spike blanks or experimental samples).

steps.title: Add Extraction Solvents
steps.instruction: Adjust the acetonitrile volume to a total of 2 mL per sample:

substeps.instruction: Add 1.9 mL of acetonitrile to method blanks.
Add 1.8 mL of acetonitrile to the Reference Standard, OPR tubes, and experimental samples.

steps.title: Phase Separation and Extraction
steps.instruction: Perform initial extraction and phase separation:

substeps.instruction: Add 1 mL of Milli-Q water (20 mΩ) into the tube.
Cap and vortex for 1 min.
Centrifuge at 3,000 rpm (1811 x g) for 5 min.

steps.title: Clean-up via dSPE
steps.instruction: Transfer 1 mL of the acetonitrile phase (top layer) to a dSPE tube (150 mg MgSO4 / 50 mg CEC 18, UCT, CUMC182CT), ensuring no solids are transferred.

steps.title: Sample Storage
steps.instruction: Transfer 500 µL of each sample to corresponding prelabeled GC vials and store capped at ambient temperature overnight.

steps.title: Concentration and Internal Standard Addition
steps.instruction: Evaporate samples to dryness under a gentle stream of nitrogen, then add the internal standard and solvent:

substeps.instruction: Add 200 µL of 0.125 µL/mL deltamethrin in ethyl acetate (internal standard) to all GC vials (25 ng per sample).
Add 800 µL ethyl acetate to all GC vials.

steps.title: GC-μECD Analysis
steps.instruction: Analyze the samples and an ethyl acetate solvent blank on an Agilent GC with a μECD using the following parameters:

substeps.instruction: Temperature program: 50 °C (hold 1 min) → 15 °/min to 220 °C → 1 °/min to 240 °C (hold 12 min) → 15 °/min to 280 °C (hold 10 min).
Helium carrier gas flow rate: 1.0 mL/min.
Inlet temperature: 240 °C.
Detector temperature: 300 °C.
Make-up flow: 60 mL/min.

steps.title: Data Integration and Quantification
steps.instruction: Integrate all chromatograms (including reference standard) using ChemStation software and export data from QUANTTAB.CSV into the provided MS Excel document for quantification.

substeps.instruction: Calculate Relative Retention Time (RRT), Relative Response Factor (RRF), mass of analyte [ng], and surrogate recovery (SURR recovery) using the provided formulas.
Adjust target analyte mass for SURR recovery if appropriate.
